content.comment_body: Hello, I am attempting to program a message block to show the output status of a function block. However, I can't seem to display the block within the message text block as I can with the relay coil or flag outputs. I have attached screenshots and the program file for reference. Any advice is appreciated.
Try closing the open outputs of your function blocks with an available terminal, then it should work.

Thank you for your response. I tried your suggestion, but it didn't work for me as it did for you. Could you advise on what else I can try? Is it necessary to reinstall the software to resolve this? I will attach the file here—could you please open it on your computer and check if you are able to make changes? I appreciate your help and sorry for the inconvenience.
Which controller version or order number are you using?
Sorry if my answer wasn't clear. I'm using the [product_name], and the part number is [article_no]. Does that provide the information you need?
I've downloaded your file and tested it. The message text feature is present. Please see the attached video for details. I'm not sure what else to suggest.

Thank you for sharing the video. I understand the file works, but my issue is that I placed a flag inside the message text block to show the function block's output. In your earlier image, your setup included the function block output directly. I'm unable to do this. I'll attach both images here to clarify my point. Thanks again for your help.

I don't usually work with LAD, as I find it has too many limitations. I translated your program to FBD, edited the message text there, and then converted it back to LAD as required by the state name. After creating your program in LAD, I also couldn't find the state name for the latching relay. Perhaps someone with more LAD experience can help.

Thanks very much for your reply. I tried converting the program from LAD to FBD and successfully placed the function block output in the message text block. Returning the program to LAD preserved the message text block content. I appreciate your assistance.
Tip: Avoid using LAD for programming; use FBD instead. LAD doesn't offer all the capabilities, and some features won't work. FBD allows for better management of your program.

(OFF TOPIC) [company_name] included LAD support to claim ladder functionality, but there are other smart relay devices that outperform in LAD programming. Most people wanting to program such devices would choose different versions if they were aware. Unfortunately, local institutions supported by [company_name] teach LAD programming on the [product_name], which means we often have to retrain students in FBD when they join us for practical experience. While the hardware platform is good, the integration of LAD and [product_name] does not work optimally. Ultimately, LAD on the [product_name] is not our choice, and [company_name] could have implemented it better.

Personally, I avoid programming the [product_name] in LAD, as it leads to too many errors. The problem with missing state names in the message text is now clear from this discussion. From other forums, I know that some programs couldn't be transferred because blocks weren't completed or visible in LAD. Translating programs to FBD revealed these blocks, allowing them to be fixed before converting back to LAD and transferring to the [product_name].

analysis.insight_summary: The user struggled to insert the output of a function block into a message text block using [product_name] software and hardware. Through community help, it was clarified that this difficulty arises specifically when using the LAD (Ladder Diagram) programming language, which has certain feature limitations. When the user translated their project into FBD (Function Block Diagram), the desired functionality was available and worked as expected. Multiple contributors confirmed that these limitations in LAD can affect the flexibility and usability of the programming environment.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to display the output of a function block within a message text block, regardless of whether LAD or FBD is used in [product_name] software.
